title: Introducing the FMF Jailbreak Rating Framework for Frontier Cyber Threats
headline: Frontier Model Forum releases Jailbreak Rating Framework for cyber threats
summary: The Frontier Model Forum has released Version 1.0 of its Jailbreak Rating Framework, which provides a structured methodology for assessing the risk profile of cyber-related model jailbreaks. The framework uses a tiered approach to evaluate capability gain, scope, and ease of deployment to help organizations prioritize security patching. It aims to create a consistent, evidence-based standard for the industry to interpret and respond to AI-related cyber threats.
why_it_matters: This framework provides Australian organisations and security teams with a standardised, industry-backed methodology to consistently evaluate and prioritise the severity of AI model jailbreaks, enabling more efficient allocation of security resources.

quotes.text: The framework uses a tiered assessment methodology that combines scores across four categories: capability gain, capability scope, ease of deployment, and ease of discovery.
This framework provides an important shared approach so that organizations can assess jailbreaks consistently and focus efforts on the highest-risk issues first.
The Frontier Model Forum’s new framework gives the industry a shared, evidence-based way to rate how serious a cyber bypass is, so teams can focus on what matters most.

dates_mentioned.quote: To that end, we are opening a public comment period through December 21, 2026.

classification.significance_reason: The framework establishes a common industry standard for assessing AI cyber-security risks, which is likely to influence global best practices adopted by Australian organisations.
classification.closing_date_quote: To that end, we are opening a public comment period through December 21, 2026.
